repair_design.summary: Use invocation-local latches and the existing per-client closed state, safely publish readyState with volatile semantics, and bound every asynchronous wait.
repair_design.assertion_fidelity: All original state assertions remain; connection and callback waits now have explicit bounds.
repair_design.causal_race: onClose/countDownLatch publication occurs before WebSocketImpl publishes ReadyState.CLOSED.
repair_design.invocation_scope: Both latches and both WebSocketClient instances are local to one test invocation.
repair_design.wait: Monotonic-deadline polling with interruptible TimeUnit.sleep and a five-second bound.

multi_writer.reason: The repair adds no counter or compound update; the existing readyState assignments are volatile writes.

state_leakage.reason: No separate state-leakage check was recorded; invocation scope is covered by the repaired design and reused-JVM gate.

causal_conclusion: The same confirmed 100 ms trigger failed all five unpatched controls and passed all five repaired runs.
claim_boundary: One manually designed repair for FS014; this does not estimate effectiveness on other cases.

source_ledger.transformation: Removed private absolute paths, timestamps, commands, raw-log paths, per-run log references, and comparison detail; retained case identity, verdicts, bounds, counted outcomes, and causal witnesses.
